articles.title: Dolly Parton’s flamboyant, fun style: ‘I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore’
articles.summary: With her gaudy rhinestones and ever mushrooming hair, the country star pioneered a new vision of femininity. Dolly Parton, country star, actor and philanthropist, dies aged 80. Dolly Parton – a life in pictures. Parton’s peerless career turned country music cliches inside out.
body: Dolly Parton ’s voluminous hair and rhinestone-festooned outfits were so essential to her fame that her quips about her appearance have become almost as well-known as her lyrics.
“It costs a lot of money to look this cheap” is perhaps her most memorable quotation, and is typical of the self-depreciating wit she employed to talk about her appearance.

She wrote about her style in her songs, too, from her 1967 hit Dumb Blonde to 2008’s Backwoods Barbie, though in reality there was nothing cheap, or dumb, about her image. With huge blond status wigs – Tennessee by way of the court of Versailles – a fondness for glitter and high heels and tightly cut clothes that showed off her exaggerated proportions, she made herself as recognizable as Coca-Cola while employing and subverting the tropes of femininity and of country music.

Parton never failed to poke fun at her own appearance. Her hair was a “fire hazard”, she would say, or “I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore” – but her look was highly deliberate. Never once did she waver from the aesthetic she described to Allure in 2020 as “gaudy, flamboyant, fun, comfortable – for me – noticeable”.
points: With her gaudy rhinestones and ever mushrooming hair, the country star pioneered a new vision of femininity.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: I sought out rejection. Instead, strangers met me with profound generosity
articles.summary: As I turned 21, fear was holding me back. So I decided to face it headfirst. It taught me that courage leads to connection – and people who owe you nothing can be astonishingly kind. In May 2024, I decided to spend 30 days getting rejected on purpose. At first, it sounded ridiculous.
body: At first, it sounded ridiculous. After all, most people spend their lives actively trying to avoid rejection – and I was deciding to walk, full force, towards it. But it had become obvious, as I turned 21, that my terror of being rejected was holding me back.

For over two years, I’d stayed in a relationship I knew wasn’t working, all too aware that the alternative – dating – would likely be riddled with rejection. On social occasions I often felt absent, focusing solely on not seeming weird or doing anything that might make others laugh at me. And in my first proper job, as a social media manager, I would talk myself out of opportunities that would put me in the spotlight and might have given me a chance to shine.
So I promised myself I’d stop hiding from rejection for one month and see what happened. After a lifetime of worrying what people thought about me, I knew that only radical action would work.
points: It taught me that courage leads to connection – and people who owe you nothing can be astonishingly kind.

articles.title: From Notting Hill to Rio: The Brand Guide to Carnival
articles.summary: In 2026, audiences are quick to call out a culture vulture. Brands wanting to engage with Carnival, Fête De La Musique, and cultural festivities must approach with caution, envisioning themselves as supporters, not headline sponsors.
body: In a matter of days, the streets of West London will be thronged with families, ravers, and historic sound systems for the Notting Hill Carnival (running August 30-31). Amongst them, a host of brand logos will appear at intervals, emblazoned across banners and freebies. It poses a perennial conundrum: what, if anything, makes a fitting Carnival collaboration?

A similar set of questions accompanies other public, open-air street parties across the globe, including June’s annual Fête de La Musique — which began in Paris in 1982, but now occurs across France — and Rio de Janeiro’s carnival in February. All these festivals have foundations in or close links to the Black diaspora, and so players wanting to enter the space should tread with sensitivity and humility, priming themselves with knowledge and context to develop brand-second — rather than brand-first — activations.
points: In 2026, audiences are quick to call out a culture vulture.
Brands wanting to engage with Carnival, Fête De La Musique, and cultural festivities must approach with caution, envisioning themselves as supporters, not headline sponsors.

articles.title: The row over Rutland: can England’s smallest county survive?
articles.summary: Its council is due to merge with Leicestershire’s in 2028, and some locals are incensed. Can the county hold on to its ceremonial status – and biggest selling point? Mysterious disappearances have been taking place lately in Rutland, an East Midlands pocket between Leicestershire, Lincolnshire and…
body: The area’s MP, the Conservative Alicia Kearns, is “not sure” what the motivation behind the thefts is. But they are certainly a fitting metaphor for Rutland’s disappearing status: its council is due to merge with Leicestershire county council in spring 2028.

“The joke goes: ‘Rutland is England 50 years ago,’” says Kearns when we meet at the county’s most famous landmark, the UK’s largest reservoir by surface area, Rutland Water, home to the Rutland Osprey Project. She tells me about the county’s farming community, its tradition of Friday shoots that supply the local pubs with game, its pride in local businesses. So resistant are Rutlanders to some aspects of modernity, “we were the last county to have a McDonald’s built”, she says. Even when it did finally arrive, in 2020, the decision “was really controversial”.

articles.title: A Tamil summer vegetarian feast: Cynthia Shanmugalingam’s cucumber yoghurt curry and gooseberry pickle
articles.summary: Serve this cold curry with a hot, fenugreek-flavoured preserve for a seasonal refresher. This lovely summery “curry” is a cold, refreshing dish from Karnataka in India, and is eaten widely in Tamil Nadu, just 20 miles across the Palk Strait from my ancestral Tamil homeland in north and eastern Sri…
body: Wash the gooseberries well, then spread them out on a cloth and leave to dry.

Put the vinegar, 250ml water, the sugar and salt in a saucepan and cook on a high heat until the sugar and salt have dissolved and the liquid is simmering. Add the gooseberries, turn off the heat and leave to pickle for 10 minutes.

In a small frying pan, dry roast the fenugreek for about 60 seconds, until fragrant, then leave to cool. Tip the cooled fenugreek into a small spice grinder or mortar, add the mustard seeds and crushed garlic, then blitz or grind to a paste. Scrape the mix into a small bowl, add the drained gooseberries, the oil, chilli powder and salt, then cover and put in the fridge for at least two hours.

First, make a coconut-cucumber paste. Peel the cucumbers, reserving the skins. Wrap each cucumber in clingfilm, then bash them lightly with a rolling pin. Remove the clingfilm, keeping the seeds, and cut the flesh on a slight diagonal into 1cm slices. Put a few of the chopped cucumbers, the cucumber seeds and skins into a blender, add the drained coconut, green chillies, garlic, coriander, black peppercorns and sesame seeds, then blitz smooth.

articles.title: The Rise of the Influencer-Investor
articles.summary: Creators are claiming a stake in the businesses their influence helps scale. But the promise of a bigger payday comes with financial risk — and a more complicated relationship with their audiences.
body: Alix Earle’s latest brand partnership comes with an ownership stake. This month, the influencer joined supplements startup Cymbiotika as an investor, alongside Hailey Bieber and Kendall Jenner. The formula is simple: Earle invests in the brand, promotes it to her 14.5 million cumulative followers across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, boosts its desirability and (ideally) revenues, while the brand catches the eyes of potential acquirers or investors.
Sofia Richie Grainge just invested in Dolce Glow, a year after becoming an investor and founding curator at ShopMy.
In May, Charli XCX became a shareholder and global ambassador at London technology startup Nothing.

articles.title: How to Party Like a Local in Mykonos, According to a Seasoned Veteran
articles.summary: A lifelong regular’s guide to choosing the right coast, landing in the part of the venue you meant to book, and getting home before the taxis disappear.
body: The sun starts to set on Little Venice and its windmills in Mykonos Town, one of many popular vistas on the island.

Now craft beer is brewed on the island, and casual Chora bars pour proper cocktails into paper cups and send revelers off into the night. Greek musicians share the calendar with international DJs, periodically reminding Mykonos of which country it belongs to. The familiar bottle-service caricature leaves out the drag stages of the old port and the smaller rooms where a night can change direction without a reservation. Prices remain high and the roads maddening, but few Mediterranean islands offer so many convincing ways to reach sunrise. After enough summers on both sides of the nap, I have settled on seven rules that every visitor needs to know.
Many of the outdoor tables in Little Venice are just inches from the tide.
points: A lifelong regular’s guide to choosing the right coast, landing in the part of the venue you meant to book, and getting home before the taxis disappear.

articles.title: Roger Federer Reflects on His Hall-of-Fame Career
articles.summary: Ahead of a starry exhibition match at Arthur Ashe, Federer chats with Vogue about his Tennis Hall of Fame induction, his own estimation of his legendary career, the state of tennis today.
body: When I roll up to the flagship of On, the Swiss shoe company, in Manhattan’s Flatiron neighborhood, I find scores of schoolkids queued up outside. Many are holding tennis rackets and tennis balls with the dream of having them signed by the man many call the greatest to ever play the game: Roger Federer.

The newest inductee to the International Tennis Hall of Fame (alongside broadcaster Mary Carillo)—the festivities are this coming weekend in Newport, Rhode Island—he has been all over New York in the last few days, launching a limited-edition version of On’s The Roger shoe (with a grass-colored sockliner and some intriguing Easter eggs that we’ll let you discover on your own) and attracting another huge throng of fans yesterday at Arthur Ashe Stadium, merely to witness him warming up on the court with Lorenzo Musetti.

Vogue: Before we get into the Hall of Fame and talk about the exhibition, I wanted to ask you about your so-called retirement. Do you feel retired? Is your life different now? You seem pretty busy to me.
points: Ahead of a starry exhibition match at Arthur Ashe, Federer chats with Vogue about his Tennis Hall of Fame induction, his own estimation of his legendary career, the state of tennis today.

articles.title: 6 Fall Denim Trends to Shop Now, According to Experts
articles.summary: Are skinny jeans back? Is low-rise here to stay? From Agolde to Frame to Ossou, we tapped experts to weigh in on the top fall denim trends of 2026.
body: Although a seasonless category, denim is a serious power player in the fall capsule wardrobe, serving as outfit building blocks as the cooler temperatures hit. New jeans are always a smart buy as you start transitioning your wardrobe to greet the shift in season. And although we’ve seen plenty of trends emerge over the past year, fall 2026 denim trends carry several spring themes forward, from bootcut to deep indigo washes to colored denim. However, the pendulum is beginning to swing: Slouchier wide-leg proportions of the past are making room for streamlined silhouettes, with straight-leg and slim cigarette styles coming back into focus.

With a little help from the experts at some of the most beloved denim brands —Levi’s, Citizens of Humanity, Still Here, and Agolde, to name a few—we’re unpacking the jean styles you should be investing in for fall 2026. Spoiler alert: Many of them are bona fide closet classics, which means they won’t feel too out of touch with the pairs you might already hold near and dear.

articles.title: This Ultra-Wide Samsung Gaming Monitor Is $650 Off (and Comes With a $120 Amazon Gift Card)
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. An ultra-wide curved gaming monitor with ridiculous specs is every gamer's dream, but they (usually) don't come cheap.
body: The Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 Series is not a regular ultra-wide gaming monitor. It has impressive specs, but you'll need a top-notch gaming computer with specific outputs to take full advantage of its 240Hz refresh rate potential.

This monitor came out in 2023 with an "excellent" review from PCMag, mainly due to its impressive 7,680 by 2,160 4K native resolution, the ridiculous 57-inch screen size, its great color range and accuracy, the 240Hz refresh rate, and its design. The VA panel also means you get a bright 1,000-nit screen. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use a DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful modern graphics card that is able to push the frames at a native resolution to max out the monitor's potential.

Although it is pricey, this monitor is a great value for the right gamer. You'll need plenty of space to fit a 57-inch screen, as well as a powerful computer to justify using the monitor—if you're not a competitive gamer with a powerful computer, it's probably not worth the price tag. Instead, consider this Asus gaming monitor going for $449.99 (originally $499) right now.
